subject: Freeze the exact least-privilege simulation input before executing the read-only effective-permission gate.
observed_facts: The validated Terraform plan contains exactly 49 create operations and zero update, delete or replace operations.

The static package declares one IAM permissions boundary, nine roles, nine inline role policies, three KMS keys, three KMS aliases, three Object-Lock-enabled S3 buckets and their configuration resources, one empty Secrets Manager container with a resource policy, and one CloudTrail trail.
The provider uses mandatory default tags on taggable resources.
The HCL defines the intended state but does not by itself prove every provider read-after-create, waiter, tagging, existence-check or normalization API call.
Authorization 127 proved that successful invocation of the IAM simulator and an allowed result for a simulated action are distinct conditions.
reasoning: A least-privilege gate that simulates only obvious create actions can produce a misleading PASS while Terraform later fails on a required read, tag, waiter or configuration API call.
Therefore the simulation matrix must include both normative mutations and all provider auxiliary calls for the pinned provider behavior.
Because the prior plan was executed with refresh=false and its detailed plan and trace were intentionally deleted, the repository currently lacks authoritative evidence for the auxiliary call set.

Fail-closed treatment is required: no read-only gate execution should be authorized until the auxiliary matrix is mapped from the provider 6.56.0 primary source or a separately authorized non-mutating trace method.
future_pass_conditions: Every provider action is mapped to an exact resource template or documented wildcard necessity.
Every policy condition key needed by the intended boundary or identity policy is supplied.
Read-after-create and tagging actions are included.
Organizations SCP/RCP applicability and session-policy status are declared.
No mutation is required to discover the matrix.
The resulting matrix is reproducible and version-pinned.
